Updated read incorporating SLOOS: Cautiously constructive on macro, but SLOOS signals persistent credit headwinds that temper any dovish take. The FOMC holds a restrictive stance (5.25–5.50% and continued runoff: $60B Treasuries, $35B agency MBS) while judging risks to employment and inflation more balanced. However, SLOOS points to ongoing tightening and softer credit demand that can weigh on growth and amplify sectoral risks:

- C&I credit: Large banks report weaker demand for C&I loans; banks continue to report on tighter standards and reduced credit line usage appetite, citing economic outlook and risk considerations.
- CRE: Large and foreign banks report tighter standards for CRE loans; CRE remains a focal vulnerability (especially office).
- RRE/Households: Standards unchanged for GSE-eligible mortgages but tighter for non-QM/jumbo categories; auto loan standards tightened for households.
- Risk metrics and drivers: Banks cite the economic outlook, risk tolerance, liquidity and capital positions, and supervisory/industry factors as reasons for tightening; banks continue to monitor delinquencies and charge-offs.
- Market structure/liquidity: Implementation tools (IORB 5.4%, ON RRP 5.3%, standing repo) support money market control but do not offset structural fragilities.

Implication: SLOOS corroborates restrictive financial conditions and softer loan appetite, reinforcing a cautious policy stance and arguing against a more dovish interpretation despite balanced inflation/employment risks. Net tone shifts slightly closer to neutral versus the prior read.
